newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht up late after devaluation idea debunked.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht up late after devaluation idea debunked.

text.p: The Thai baht strengthened against the dollar in late trade on Tuesday on heavy dollar selling after the Bank of Thailand firmly ruled out any baht devaluation, dealers said.

"There was already some selling of the dollar in the morning. The central bank's statement triggered more selling of the U.S. unit in both spot and the swap markets," said one dealer at a European bank.
The baht was traded at 26.025/26.030 to the dollar in late trade on Tuesday against 26.045/26.055 in the early morning, dealers said.
It added that the baht was not fundamentally overvalued and a devaluation would do more harm than good to overall economy.

"The BOT therefore remains firmly committed to maintaining the integrity of Thailand's current exchange rate regime which has been and will continue to be an appropriate system for Thailand," the central bank said.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the mid-rate unchanged at 25.99 against the dollar.
The overnight interbank rate fell to 12.00-13.00 percent in late trade from 15.00-16.00 on easing demand for funds to invest in the dollar and baht/dollar swap premiums, dealers said.
Dealers said the rising sentiment for the baht also made banks more willing to lend funds in the market.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium eased to 15.50/16.50 satangs per a dollar late from 16.75/17.50 early, dealers said.
